speaker: io
say: The road’s gone cold, Kore. Roads don’t do that.
words_shown: The road’s gone cold, Kore. Roads don’t do that.
tone: Troubled, her hand flat on the ground.

speaker: io
say: Show us the first one.
words_shown: Show us the first one.
tone: Kind and practical, already rolling up her sleeves.

speaker: io
say: I’ll light it with something small. Something I can tend.
words_shown: I’ll light it with something small. Something I can tend.
tone: Careful and gentle, cupping a flame.

speaker: io
say: There. Feel it? Warm.
words_shown: There. Feel it? Warm.
tone: Soft and pleased, her hands around the warmth.

speaker: io
say: It’s not the same as holding on, Kore.
words_shown: It’s not the same as holding on, Kore.
tone: Gentle, a little defensive. She has heard the question.

speaker: io
say: I came here as a girl. It was louder.
words_shown: I came here as a girl. It was louder.
tone: Wistful, a small smile at the memory.

speaker: io
say: Hello, Marta.
words_shown: Hello, Marta.
tone: Soft. A girl again for a moment.

speaker: io
say: Her bed’s by the window. It always was.
words_shown: Her bed’s by the window. It always was.
tone: Soft, standing very still.

speaker: io
say: Keep them made, Marta.
words_shown: Keep them made, Marta.
tone: Gentle and firm. She cannot let go either.

speaker: io
say: You keep saying that.
words_shown: You keep saying that.
tone: Half teasing, half touched.

speaker: io
say: My letters. Kore, they’re folding themselves.
words_shown: My letters. Kore, they’re folding themselves.
tone: Astonished, a little frightened.

speaker: io
say: I never meant them to fly.
words_shown: I never meant them to fly.
tone: Small and bewildered.

speaker: io
say: Marta’s still at the window.
words_shown: Marta’s still at the window.
tone: Looking back, soft.

speaker: io
say: I’ll write to her. And this time I’ll send it.
words_shown: I’ll write to her. And this time I’ll send it.
tone: A small promise to herself, surprised by it.

speaker: kore
say: [laughs] Cold. I hate the cold. It’s so final.
words_shown: Cold. I hate the cold. It’s so final.
tone: A shiver turned into a joke. She knows more about final than anyone.

speaker: kore
say: Then something’s making it.
words_shown: Then something’s making it.
tone: Quiet, the joke gone out of her.

speaker: kore
say: Small is good. Small doesn’t get ideas.
words_shown: Small is good. Small doesn’t get ideas.
tone: Wry. A true thing dressed as a joke.

speaker: kore
say: You’re good at that. Keeping things lit.
words_shown: You’re good at that. Keeping things lit.
tone: Fond, with a question hidden in it.

speaker: kore
say: Isn’t it?
words_shown: Isn’t it?
tone: Very light. Not an argument. Leave it hanging.

speaker: kore
say: I can’t see how one of them ends. Not one.
words_shown: I can’t see how one of them ends. Not one.
tone: Almost to herself. Puzzled, and starting to be afraid.

speaker: kore
say: Then tonight, we hold it.
words_shown: Then tonight, we hold it.
tone: Light and certain. Defending, without a laugh.

speaker: kore
say: Io, stay by the node. I’ll stand in front.
words_shown: Io, stay by the node. I’ll stand in front.
tone: Easy words, steel under them.

speaker: kore
say: I keep meaning it.
words_shown: I keep meaning it.
tone: Quiet and plain. No laugh.

speaker: kore
say: They’ve wanted to go somewhere for years.
words_shown: They’ve wanted to go somewhere for years.
tone: Gentle wonder, watching them.

speaker: kore
say: [softly] You did. You just never sent them.
words_shown: You did. You just never sent them.
tone: Tender. The truest thing she says in this zone.

speaker: kore
say: She’ll make the beds tonight. And tomorrow.
words_shown: She’ll make the beds tonight. And tomorrow.
tone: Fond and a little sad. Not a criticism.

speaker: europa
say: The threads are thicker here. Like rope.
words_shown: The threads are thicker here. Like rope.
tone: Fascinated, and less playful than usual.

speaker: europa
say: My stitches are holding, captain. Look.
words_shown: My stitches are holding, captain. Look.
tone: Proud, showing off her work on his lamps.

speaker: europa
say: Look. The warmth is leaving on a thread. North, like everything.
words_shown: Look. The warmth is leaving on a thread. North, like everything.
tone: Pointing, half fascinated and half annoyed.

speaker: europa
say: [playfully] There. Sewn shut. Pull all you like.
words_shown: There. Sewn shut. Pull all you like.
tone: Triumphant and teasing, to whatever is pulling.

speaker: europa
say: Warden blue on every door. Faded.
words_shown: Warden blue on every door. Faded.
tone: Softer than usual. She notices colour first, and this one is sad.

speaker: europa
say: Someone irons these. Every night, someone irons these.
words_shown: Someone irons these. Every night, someone irons these.
tone: A craftswoman’s respect, and it moves her.

speaker: europa
say: Nobody’s slept in them. Not a dent.
words_shown: Nobody’s slept in them. Not a dent.
tone: Gentle, smoothing a blanket that needs no smoothing.

speaker: europa
say: Their threads run back north. Somebody’s sending them.
words_shown: Their threads run back north. Somebody’s sending them.
tone: Sharp, worried.

speaker: europa
say: Paper wings. Oh, that’s good work.
words_shown: Paper wings. Oh, that’s good work.
tone: Delighted, a craftswoman admiring the folding.

speaker: europa
say: The road’s glowing all the way back. Like a hem.
words_shown: The road’s glowing all the way back. Like a hem.
tone: Pleased, leaning over the rail.

speaker: callisto
say: Frost on the rail. And it isn’t winter.
words_shown: Frost on the rail. And it isn’t winter.
tone: Quiet, noticing first, a little wary.

speaker: callisto
say: No birds. Not one.
words_shown: No birds. Not one.
tone: Low and flat. She has been listening.

speaker: callisto
say: Quick. Something’s watching from the trees.
words_shown: Quick. Something’s watching from the trees.
tone: Low and fast, a hand on her bow.

speaker: callisto
say: Two more. The road’s waiting.
words_shown: Two more. The road’s waiting.
tone: Calm, moving them on.

speaker: callisto
say: Every chimney lit, and half the windows dark.
words_shown: Every chimney lit, and half the windows dark.
tone: Quiet observation, taking in the town.

speaker: callisto
say: Forty beds. Every one turned down.
words_shown: Forty beds. Every one turned down.
tone: Quiet, taking it in.

speaker: callisto
say: Three of them, coming up the hill. Slow.
words_shown: Three of them, coming up the hill. Slow.
tone: Low and level, counting them.

speaker: callisto
say: Now.
words_shown: Now.
tone: One word, exactly on time. The moment.

speaker: callisto
say: That one’s waiting, Io. For you to let it go.
words_shown: That one’s waiting, Io. For you to let it go.
tone: Quiet, almost reverent.

speaker: callisto
say: North-east. The lean’s stronger.
words_shown: North-east. The lean’s stronger.
tone: Calm, eyes ahead.

speaker: captain
say: Raiders. Low on the left. Hold on to something that isn’t me.
words_shown: Raiders. Low on the left. Hold on to something that isn’t me.
tone: Clipped and calm under fire. A dry joke at the end.

speaker: captain
say: That’s them seen off. Nobody touch the lamps.
words_shown: That’s them seen off. Nobody touch the lamps.
tone: Breathing out, straight back to business.

speaker: captain
say: Sunstone’s sulking in this cold. We set down here till the roads warm.
words_shown: Sunstone’s sulking in this cold. We set down here till the roads warm.
tone: Flat, cross with the weather, not with them.

speaker: captain
say: There’s an old Warden by the fire who knows the road. Ask him.
words_shown: There’s an old Warden by the fire who knows the road. Ask him.
tone: Short, pointing with his chin.

speaker: captain
say: She won’t lift on cold stone. Neither would I.
words_shown: She won’t lift on cold stone. Neither would I.
tone: Dry, patting the rail.

speaker: captain
say: Feel that? One stone lit, and she’s humming.
words_shown: Feel that? One stone lit, and she’s humming.
tone: Pleased in spite of himself.

speaker: captain
say: All three lit and she’s warm to the hand. Go and see Dawnroost. I’ll wait.
words_shown: All three lit and she’s warm to the hand. Go and see Dawnroost. I’ll wait.
tone: Satisfied, waving them on.

speaker: captain
say: Dawnroost was a proud town. Still is. It just hasn’t noticed it’s empty.
words_shown: Dawnroost was a proud town. Still is. It just hasn’t noticed it’s empty.
tone: Quiet and respectful, a little sad.

speaker: captain
say: Wraiths at night, they say. Don’t be heroes. Be back.
words_shown: Wraiths at night, they say. Don’t be heroes. Be back.
tone: Gruff care, kept short.

speaker: captain
say: Warm stone under her. We can fly. North-east, where they lean.
words_shown: Warm stone under her. We can fly. North-east, where they lean.
tone: Decided. A captain giving the course.

speaker: captain
say: The flames lean harder here than at the lake. We’re closer.
words_shown: The flames lean harder here than at the lake. We’re closer.
tone: Uneasy, reading the sky.

speaker: captain
say: Marta fed you. I can tell. You’re walking slower.
words_shown: Marta fed you. I can tell. You’re walking slower.
tone: Deadpan teasing.

speaker: captain
say: Won again. You’ll be wanting a medal. I haven’t got one.
words_shown: Won again. You’ll be wanting a medal. I haven’t got one.
tone: Dry and fond.

speaker: captain
say: Bad night. There’s blankets in the hold.
words_shown: Bad night. There’s blankets in the hold.
tone: Gruff kindness, no fuss.

speaker: captain
say: Back by morning.
words_shown: Back by morning.
tone: Called after them, half an order.

speaker: captain
say: Cold like this isn’t weather. Weather moves. This just sits.
words_shown: Cold like this isn’t weather. Weather moves. This just sits.
tone: Low. A sailor’s unease.

speaker: roadwarden
say: Put your hand flat on the road. Feel that? It’s never once been cold.
words_shown: Put your hand flat on the road. Feel that? It’s never once been cold.
tone: Gruff and urgent, an old man showing strangers a wound.

speaker: roadwarden
say: Three of the road stones have gone dark between here and Dawnroost. Light them again.
words_shown: Three of the road stones have gone dark between here and Dawnroost. Light them again.
tone: Plain. A request he hates having to make.

speaker: roadwarden
say: The warmth is leaving the road. I can feel it running north under my hand.
words_shown: The warmth is leaving the road. I can feel it running north under my hand.
tone: Slow, feeling it under his palm. What he feels, not what he knows.

speaker: roadwarden
say: One by the bridge. One in the standing stones, off to the west. One up on the rise.
words_shown: One by the bridge. One in the standing stones, off to the west. One up on the rise.
tone: Directions counted off on his fingers, clear and slow.

speaker: roadwarden
say: That’s one lit. I felt it come on, from here.
words_shown: That’s one lit. I felt it come on, from here.
tone: Wonder he tries to hide. A hand pressed to the ground.

speaker: roadwarden
say: All three lit. Go on to Dawnroost. Marta will want to feed you.
words_shown: All three lit. Go on to Dawnroost. Marta will want to feed you.
tone: Relieved and gruffly proud, sending them off.

speaker: roadwarden
say: I should have gone north with them. The forty.
words_shown: I should have gone north with them. The forty.
tone: Low. It costs him to say it.

speaker: roadwarden
say: I was afraid. So I kept the road instead. Eight years, on my own.
words_shown: I was afraid. So I kept the road instead. Eight years, on my own.
tone: Plain, no excuse in it. A small breath before the last words.

speaker: roadwarden
say: Dawnroost’s node is the last one that burns by itself. The rest feed off it.
words_shown: Dawnroost’s node is the last one that burns by itself. The rest feed off it.
tone: Grave. A Warden explaining a duty.

speaker: roadwarden
say: Warm. Feel it. Not like it was, but warm.
words_shown: Warm. Feel it. Not like it was, but warm.
tone: Quiet joy, his hand flat on the stone. Let the last word glow.

speaker: roadwarden
say: I’ll keep it through the dark. A road wants keeping, moon or no moon.
words_shown: I’ll keep it through the dark. A road wants keeping, moon or no moon.
tone: Settled and steady. A man who has found his work again.

speaker: roadwarden
say: Marta still makes up their beds, I hear. Forty. I can’t go and look.
words_shown: Marta still makes up their beds, I hear. Forty. I can’t go and look.
tone: Ashamed and tender.

speaker: roadwarden
say: Hot hands, all four. You’ve been fighting. Lend the road some.
words_shown: Hot hands, all four. You’ve been fighting. Lend the road some.
tone: Dry humour, a little admiring.

speaker: roadwarden
say: Sit by the fire. Not the stone, the fire. The stone’s got nothing to give yet.
words_shown: Sit by the fire. Not the stone, the fire. The stone’s got nothing to give yet.
tone: Gentle, fussing in his gruff way.

speaker: roadwarden
say: You four walk like Wardens now. I don’t say that lightly.
words_shown: You four walk like Wardens now. I don’t say that lightly.
tone: Solemn praise.

speaker: roadwarden
say: Keep to the stones.
words_shown: Keep to the stones.
tone: Called after them. An old habit of command.

speaker: carter
say: Sunstone. A whole cart of it, and not one would warm a teacup.
words_shown: Sunstone. A whole cart of it, and not one would warm a teacup.
tone: Comic despair, slapping the cart.

speaker: carter
say: Sunstone sulks when something else is hungrier for the warm. Up north, I reckon.
words_shown: Sunstone sulks when something else is hungrier for the warm. Up north, I reckon.
tone: A trader’s hunch, half to himself.

speaker: carter
say: The old Warden at the camp knows these stones. Back down the road, by the fire.
words_shown: The old Warden at the camp knows these stones. Back down the road, by the fire.
tone: Helpful, pointing with his whip.

speaker: carter
say: The stones are lit and my cart’s glowing. I’ll stay till morning, just to be warm.
words_shown: The stones are lit and my cart’s glowing. I’ll stay till morning, just to be warm.
tone: Content, a little lazy.

speaker: carter
say: I’ll take this load south, where they’ll need it. It’s going to be a long dark.
words_shown: I’ll take this load south, where they’ll need it. It’s going to be a long dark.
tone: Practical, then quieter on the last sentence.

speaker: carter
say: Keep warm, you four.
words_shown: Keep warm, you four.
tone: Called after them, friendly.

speaker: marta
say: Io? Little Io? Look at you. You’ve got her walk.
words_shown: Io? Little Io? Look at you. You’ve got her walk.
tone: Astonished joy, then a catch on the last words.

speaker: marta
say: The beds are made up. Forty of them. Sleep in any you like.
words_shown: The beds are made up. Forty of them. Sleep in any you like.
tone: Brisk to cover tears. A hostess at once.

speaker: marta
say: I make them every night. Forty bunks, fresh linen. Somebody has to.
words_shown: I make them every night. Forty bunks, fresh linen. Somebody has to.
tone: Matter-of-fact and proud, a little stubborn.

speaker: marta
say: Halcyon slept by the window. Always cold, always wanted the window. The end one’s hers.
words_shown: Halcyon slept by the window. Always cold, always wanted the window. The end one’s hers.
tone: Fond, remembering, smiling.

speaker: marta
say: The cold lights come in at night and look at the beds. Like they’re hoping one’s theirs.
words_shown: The cold lights come in at night and look at the beds. Like they’re hoping one’s theirs.
tone: Low and puzzled, more sad than frightened. Her guess.

speaker: marta
say: Every night something comes up the hill for the node behind the hall. Wraiths.
words_shown: Every night something comes up the hill for the node behind the hall. Wraiths.
tone: Plain and grim, then flat on the last word.

speaker: marta
say: We’ve held it with buckets of coals and prayers. We’re running out of both.
words_shown: We’ve held it with buckets of coals and prayers. We’re running out of both.
tone: Dry and tired. A joke to stay standing.

speaker: marta
say: Up the hill behind the hall. You’ll see it burning. It’s the only thing that is.
words_shown: Up the hill behind the hall. You’ll see it burning. It’s the only thing that is.
tone: Clear directions, a hand pointing up the hill.

speaker: marta
say: Io. Should I stop making the beds? Tell me and I’ll stop.
words_shown: Io. Should I stop making the beds? Tell me and I’ll stop.
tone: Quiet, almost hoping to be told.

speaker: marta
say: I’ll keep making them. Until somebody tells me different.
words_shown: I’ll keep making them. Until somebody tells me different.
tone: Stubborn and warm, a small smile.

speaker: marta
say: The road’s warm again. I’ve aired every bed.
words_shown: The road’s warm again. I’ve aired every bed.
tone: Bright and busy, pleased.

speaker: marta
say: Io, you two raced up these stairs. She always let you win. You never noticed.
words_shown: Io, you two raced up these stairs. She always let you win. You never noticed.
tone: Tender and teasing, a story she has told herself many times.

speaker: marta
say: Forty went north with her. Forty good boots on that floor. I can still hear them.
words_shown: Forty went north with her. Forty good boots on that floor. I can still hear them.
tone: Hushed. Hearing it.

speaker: marta
say: So the old fool’s still keeping the road. Tell him he can come up for his supper.
words_shown: So the old fool’s still keeping the road. Tell him he can come up for his supper.
tone: Exasperated affection.

speaker: marta
say: Tamsin wants to be a Warden. I haven’t the heart to tell her there aren’t any.
words_shown: Tamsin wants to be a Warden. I haven’t the heart to tell her there aren’t any.
tone: Soft, a sigh in it.

speaker: marta
say: Brann counts the stores twice a day. As if they’ll grow.
words_shown: Brann counts the stores twice a day. As if they’ll grow.
tone: Dry and fond.

speaker: marta
say: You’re bleeding on my floor. Sit. No, not on the clean bed.
words_shown: You’re bleeding on my floor. Sit. No, not on the clean bed.
tone: Bossy and quick, not unkind.

speaker: marta
say: Into a bed, all four. Any one. They’re made.
words_shown: Into a bed, all four. Any one. They’re made.
tone: Firm and tender. Her beds have a use at last.

speaker: marta
say: You look like the new ones always looked. Too thin and too sure.
words_shown: You look like the new ones always looked. Too thin and too sure.
tone: Wry, remembering.

speaker: marta
say: You’ve the look of the forty now. I don’t know if that’s good.
words_shown: You’ve the look of the forty now. I don’t know if that’s good.
tone: Proud and uneasy at once.

speaker: marta
say: Wipe your feet!
words_shown: Wipe your feet!
tone: Called after them, sharp. A habit.

speaker: marta
say: You held it. All night. The forty couldn’t have done better. Don’t tell them I said so.
words_shown: You held it. All night. The forty couldn’t have done better. Don’t tell them I said so.
tone: Glowing, then a conspirator’s whisper on the last sentence.

speaker: brann
say: Stores are for Wardens. You’re not Wardens. Take what you need anyway.
words_shown: Stores are for Wardens. You’re not Wardens. Take what you need anyway.
tone: Blunt, then giving way.

speaker: brann
say: Cold lights in the stores last night, poking at the lamp oil. Thirsty, I’d say.
words_shown: Cold lights in the stores last night, poking at the lamp oil. Thirsty, I’d say.
tone: A storekeeper’s suspicion. His guess.

speaker: brann
say: The road stones went dark one by one. I wrote down the days. Nobody’s asked to see.
words_shown: The road stones went dark one by one. I wrote down the days. Nobody’s asked to see.
tone: Gruff, a little hurt.

speaker: brann
say: Marta’s in the hall. Big door, smoke from every chimney. She’ll want to feed you.
words_shown: Marta’s in the hall. Big door, smoke from every chimney. She’ll want to feed you.
tone: Plain directions.

speaker: brann
say: Forty sets of everything, and nobody to wear them. I oil the buckles anyway.
words_shown: Forty sets of everything, and nobody to wear them. I oil the buckles anyway.
tone: Quiet and steady, sad underneath.

speaker: brann
say: The rule was nobody goes north without spare socks. They all took socks. I counted.
words_shown: The rule was nobody goes north without spare socks. They all took socks. I counted.
tone: Deadpan, with grief under the joke.

speaker: brann
say: Node’s held. I’ve opened a cask I was saving. Don’t tell Marta which one.
words_shown: Node’s held. I’ve opened a cask I was saving. Don’t tell Marta which one.
tone: Gruff glee.

speaker: brann
say: Bring back what you borrow.
words_shown: Bring back what you borrow.
tone: Called after them, half serious.

speaker: tamsin
say: Halt! Who goes there? I’m a Warden. Nearly.
words_shown: Halt! Who goes there? I’m a Warden. Nearly.
tone: Fierce, then honest.

speaker: tamsin
say: The cold lights are Wardens who forgot their way home. That’s what I think.
words_shown: The cold lights are Wardens who forgot their way home. That’s what I think.
tone: Certain, the way children are.

speaker: tamsin
say: Marta’s in the hall. She’ll make you eat. Everybody has to.
words_shown: Marta’s in the hall. She’ll make you eat. Everybody has to.
tone: Matter-of-fact, a little put upon.

speaker: tamsin
say: I sleep in the end bed when Marta isn’t looking. It’s the best one. It’s by the window.
words_shown: I sleep in the end bed when Marta isn’t looking. It’s the best one. It’s by the window.
tone: Conspiratorial, proud of her secret.

speaker: tamsin
say: I saw you hold the node. I’m going to be a Warden. A real one.
words_shown: I saw you hold the node. I’m going to be a Warden. A real one.
tone: Breathless and decided.

speaker: tamsin
say: I’m guarding this bit!
words_shown: I’m guarding this bit!
tone: Shouted after them, very serious.
